quest.title: The Reason We Are Gathered Here
quest.description: Everything is ready and now it's up to Nilou's performance in the debate.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Praxis x5, Unknown Item #363328 x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Wait for the debate two days later (15:00 – 18:00)

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Hello and welcome, everyone. I am Safwan, a scholar from the Akademiya, and I will serve as this debate's adjudicator.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: I swear to judge both parties with the utmost wisdom and impartiality. I will neither interfere with the proceedings nor demonstrate bias.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: I ask for both parties to stand. May the Dendro Archon also serve as a witness to this duel of wits.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Since you so desperately demand an explanation, I will expound on the Akademiya's stance.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: You may have misunderstood us from the outset, and believed that the Akademiya is prejudiced against you.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: However, the truth is that the Akademiya wishes for every resident of Sumeru to be afforded opportunities to grow and cultivate their wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Therefore, the works they consume should also possess enlightening qualities and intellectual value.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: We have failed to identify these qualities in the shows performed at Zubayr Theater.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: In other words, instead of struggling against the Akademiya in pointless confrontations, if you had spent your time reflecting on improving the quality of your shows and enlightening your audience...

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Zubayr Theater would not be today facing such a tragic fate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aggressive from the get-go. He's really putting on the pressure...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can Nilou stand her ground?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Calm down, Nilou... First, carefully analyze what he said.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (He said that we were shut down not because the Akademiya looks down on the arts, but rather because our shows aren't up to their standards. However...)

talks.objective: Go to the theater and witness the debate

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (She already agreed to this. She wants to win, no matter what. Me too.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Sharif believes that interpersonal relationships are a byproduct of working towards a goal. Once that goal is achieved or abandoned, those relationships would have no more reason to continue.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Then, if someone has failed to live up to his expectations—

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: If someone has failed to live up to your expectations and ran away from home, then she shouldn't be your daughter anymore, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Inayah...

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: Sorry Nilou, as expected, I should be the one to say it. You don't need to shoulder this responsibility for me.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: If in your eyes, the purpose of my existence is to become your academic successor, then that goal has ended in complete failure.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: By your logic, that means there is no more reason to sustain our relationship as father and daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Members of the audience who do not belong to either debate party, please speak with caution.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Let her speak.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: What she does not say, Nilou will.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: No matter how many disagreements we've had, the truth is that you are still my father.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: You're so immersed in your own world that you can't understand why we come together for the sake of relationships.

dialogues.speaker: Rekhar
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't look down on us!

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: You can watch a dance anywhere, but there's only one Zubayr Theater!

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: I'm almost starting to feel sorry for this guy, what with the idiotic things he's said.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Order, order! Members of the audience, do not interrupt debate proceedings!

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I confess that this is the final argument we had prepared. Disown me, and you will win the debate.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: But before that, Father, I have some final words to say.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I've been doing some soul-searching. Not about whether I should have run away from home, but whether there was any point to my personal rebellion against you.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I kept trying to earn your approval, but I only disappointed you over and over. The truth is, I ran away from home as a means to vent my recurring frustrations.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: That is to say, I was exerting pressure on you, and hoping you'd give up on your lofty expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: But by doing that, wasn't I just doing the same thing as you?

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I won't force my expectations upon you anymore. At Zubayr Theater, I have found the life I've always wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I will move on from my family troubles and strive towards my new goal.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: But if you dare to harm this place, then I will stand with my friends here and fight against you.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: This is not the time to space out, Sharif. The debate is still underway.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: ...You already consider them to be your friends?

dialogues.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
dialogues.text: You should be asking US that question.

dialogues.speaker: Sohrin
dialogues.text: Of course we are!

dialogues.speaker: Abhi
dialogues.text: Miss Inayah is a really good friend!

dialogues.speaker: Khasani
dialogues.text: It was a bit of a process, but we won her over.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Make no mistake:

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: All those who come to Zubayr Theater become one of us. We will always be with her.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Hmph, such puerile simplicity. However...

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: It is surprisingly a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Wait, what are you...? Ah, never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: They... left?

dialogues.speaker: Rekhar
dialogues.text: Does that mean we've won?

dialogues.speaker: Kourosh
dialogues.text: We won?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou, you're amazing!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Ha... Haha...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I relaxed for a moment, and... I feel a little faint...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: It looks like he still has a place for her in his heart.

response.speaker: Sheikh Zubayr
response.text: Terrific work, Nilou and Inayah. They likely won't cause any more trouble for us.

response.speaker: Farhad
response.text: Didn't know you could get so fierce. I have a lot of newfound respect for you two.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: This really took a lot out of me, though. *sigh* I don't ever wanna do this again...

response.speaker: Sohrin
response.text: Both Miss Nilou and Miss Inayah were so cool!

response.speaker: Rekhar
response.text: Should we throw a second round of celebrations?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The curtain finally falls on the debate amidst a euphony of cheers...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Feeling any calmer?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yes, I feel a lot better. The more I think back on everything, the more surreal it all feels.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I don't think I could repeat what I did a second time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All of our preparations paid off.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yes, and it's all thanks to you.

choices.text: Now that I've heard everyone else's stories...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, I see. You mean how fate brought me to the theater, right?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Then, I'll have to tell you about my teacher, who Mr. Zubayr had mentioned.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Mr. Zubayr opened his theater when I was still a child.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: There was a beautiful dancer, and from the moment I saw her, I couldn't look away.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I thought to myself, "The gods must have blessed her with such talent."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: But later on, she would actually smile down at me and say, "Just the opposite, in fact."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The opposite?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah. She said, "Dance is an art born from toil. It isn't a gift from the gods, but a creation by our own hands."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "It is a beautiful thing born from our life experiences. Whenever there is joy or something to be celebrated, people will dance."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: "In other words, any place where people can effortlessly begin a dance will for sure be filled with the blessings of everyone's happiness."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: She wasn't looking for flowers and applause — all she wanted was to see her audience smile.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Right, the same as what Mr. Khasani believes.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I was completely moved by what she had said, so I started taking dance lessons from her. And later on, I began to dance here in her stead.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Before she retired, she told me, "For as long as you live, never forget what dance means to others."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: This is why Mr. Zubayr and I never intended to listen to the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Even though it ended up causing everyone a whole lot of trouble, thankfully, everything worked out in the end.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Mhm, although I do have a small regret.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Inayah?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah. Even though she has already decided to stop fighting with her father, they never managed to have a real conversation with each other.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Before he left, Mr. Sharif looked like he had a lot on his mind.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: He probably has a lot of things he wants to say, but will now perhaps never get a chance to.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah, but I still hope that things can change. It never hurts to have hope.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: You and Paimon are more than welcome to keep attending our shows.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, who knows, next time, you might see Inayah on the stage.

choices.text: That might be for the best.
Looks like you won't have to worry anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Everyone, I'd like to introduce you to our newest member: Inayah!

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: H—Hello, everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: She'll be dancing for us from now on, so please give her your support.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Inayah's taken her place on the stage! Paimon wonders how she'll look once she starts dancing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When you stop and think about it, happy endings like this sure aren't easy to come by!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A lot of things came together to make it happen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou's efforts, everyone's wisdom, Inayah's determination...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And Sharif's mercy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean by that?

choices.text: I think he intentionally gave us a chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You do have a point there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The whole demolition thing was going overboard, but he really could've banned Nilou and the others from dancing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he really wanted to be ruthless, he could've done some real damage, even without winning the debate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh well, it's not like we can understand how people like him think. Let's focus on watching the performance!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Wait, look who the cat dragged in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't that Inayah's father!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go greet him.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Oh, it's you two.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: I don't have much to do today, so I just came to look around this place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, are you looking for Inayah?

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: No, I am simply here to watch a performance. There is no need to trouble her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Shouldn't you be busy?

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Well, I was, for a time.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: My loss at the debate caused quite the loss of face for the Akademiya, so there was a period of unrest.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: I used this opportunity to suggest that my superiors temporarily suspend me from duty. Otherwise, the rumors would probably persist for even longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suspended from duty...

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Yes, I am temporarily unemployed. However, I now have an abundance of time, so I can afford to come here and watch a show.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: I admit that I do not understand the magic that this theater possesses, but my curiosity has been piqued.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: I still cannot forget that young lady's perseverance. Inayah would almost certainly mature in the presence of such a person.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you're still concerned about your daughter.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: There are no parents who do not worry about their children. I suppose she managed to hit a weak spot of mine.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Never mind. I do not have the right to say that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're already here, so you might as well go see her.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: No, that is not necessary. I will take my leave after the show concludes.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: ...Do not tell her that I was here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like father, like daughter. They're both so awkward with their feelings!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah, she probably would've snuck away as well if I didn't drag her back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think they'll be able to reconcile?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I'm not sure. A complete reconciliation may also not be the best thing for them right now.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: All those years of arguments and misunderstandings can't be settled overnight. It might be best if they continue to keep some distance for now.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: But no matter where their hearts and bodies may be, they will always be family.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: All I wish for them is to be able to one day tap into the warmth of that bond.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, by the way, everyone's really thankful to you for helping out with the debate.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: So we made you a little something. Hope you'll like it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I—Isn't this Zubayr Theater?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, this is amazing... It's so detailed and polished...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hee-hee, we've also never made anything this complicated before.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Mr. Zubayr and Mr. Khasani took charge of the design, while Inayah and I made all the little pieces with the help of others.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Ms. Rekhar and Miss Najia made and assembled the centerpiece.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: As adventurers, you two will doubtlessly travel to many more lands and see many more things.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: That's why we hope that your time at Zubayr Theater will become a fond memory of your journey. You two are welcome back anytime!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mhm, we'll come back and watch you dance whenever we get the chance!

choices.text: Thank you all for being so considerate.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: You're welcome, and there's no need to be so polite. You learned fast!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Come on, take it. This is the story of you and me. It's a tale that I'll never, ever forget.

choices.text: According to custom, I should drop the formalities and just accept it, right?
He didn't have to agree to the debate.

talks.objective: Go to the theater to see Inayah

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You two are welcome here anytime! Seeing you safe and sound in between adventures will keep me from worrying too much about you.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I think I already see you two as people of the Grand Bazaar. Yep, without a doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: During the debate, you said that you found a new wish. What was it?

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I actually... want to learn how to dance from Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a great wish, but with your shyness, are you really going to be okay going up on stage?

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: I—I'll try my best...

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: Nilou wasn't born an expert, either!

dialogues.speaker: Zubayr Theater Billboard
dialogues.text: Due to special circumstances, all theatrical performances have been cancelled and the resumption time has yet to be determined. Sorry about the inconvenience.

dialogues.speaker: Inayah
dialogues.text: Everything is ready. The only thing left is to wait until the day after tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hehe, I hope I'll actually be able to get some sleep over the next two nights.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: In your eyes, our shows can't meet the Akademiya's expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Shouldn't it be the audience who decides if a show is intellectual or enlightening? Why is someone from the Akademiya judging that?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Also, I believe that there is no such thing as a wiser or more enlightening performance.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Art doesn't discriminate, and it appeals to all. Everyone has the right to appreciate art.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Appreciation is but a primitive form of satisfaction. Guidance and enlightenment are necessary if we are to induce growth in the performers as well as the audience.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: This stance holds performers to a higher standard and encourages the development of the arts.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: If all performances are simple-minded, require little effort to comprehend, and lack any impetus for the betterment of society, then the people will not be able to develop a greater level of artistic understanding.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Nurturing the populace's understanding requires a long and arduous process, and guiding this process is the Akademiya's true goal.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (He changed the topic without batting an eye! Good thing I'm prepared.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (If I remember correctly, what I should say here is...)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Someone at our theater has tried that before.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: He was a famed artist, but he recognized that very few people could connect with his works.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I agree that art should be enlightening, but we can't pursue that goal by creating complicated works.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: If a work can't tap into an audience's personal experiences or feelings, then its contents may as well be a castle in the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: What's the point of performing a show that its audience can't even follow?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: That would only be forcing people to watch something they don't like.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: You can only reach that conclusion from a place of ignorance.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: In that case, before passing judgment, you should first become a better dancer than me.

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: You tell them, Nilou!

dialogues.speaker: Kourosh
dialogues.text: Looks like he's backed himself into a corner...

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: As the party holding the burden of proof, Sharif has failed to provide sufficient support for his judgment of the quality of Zubayr Theater's programs.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Likewise, the definition that Nilou put forth is but her personal opinion. Neither party is the victor for this particular point of contention.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: ...Additionally, I must request that both parties exercise greater control on their emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keep it up, Nilou! You're doing great!

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: In that case, I shall speak of more concrete matters. The essence of this issue is that you have violated the law, so you must now pay the price for your transgression.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: This course of action is also completely procedurally sound. We have already contacted Zubayr Theater multiple times regarding the theater's repertoire.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: However, you have consciously ignored our warnings — or perhaps your compliance was purely superficial. Regardless, that failure has indirectly led to the present day's proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: That is indeed so, according to the laws decreed by the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (He's started talking about procedural stuff, so I need to focus on...)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Zubayr has already provided signed copies of all documentation related to our operations. Everything is perfectly filled out and valid.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Although the theater's performances don't align with the Akademiya's requests, the law doesn't say that Zubayr Theater can be demolished only because of that reason.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Demolition notices need to be provided in writing and made available to the public. Otherwise, the theater can continue to operate as long as its license is valid.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Failing to follow these rules makes your stance procedurally unsound.

dialogues.speaker: Abhi
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Sohrin
dialogues.text: That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: ...There are different ways to apply the rules. There is precedent for this.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: So long as this matter is discussed within the Akademiya, this course of action will come to pass.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Looking at the past 27 cases of similar nature, 90% of them support Sharif's claim and position.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: However, the demolition process in those cases was only started after discussion at the Akademiya. In other words, premature notice of demolition is indeed a rash act.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: That's more than enough. We've proven that the order is unreasonable as it currently stands.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. Cease your futile resistance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou's definitely won this point, right?

choices.text: She still can't let down her guard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... Stay focused, Nilou!

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Even if permission for demolition has yet to be obtained, it is a fact that your performances violated the Akademiya's policies on numerous occasions.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Based on that fact, we can permanently revoke your right to perform in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: Safwan
response.text: Under the current system, it is indeed possible to immediately revoke Zubayr Theater's performing rights.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a thing!?

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Rather than protecting Zubayr Theater, I surmise that your true intention is to maintain your hold over your audience, and their patronage as your source of income.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: Without them, Zubayr Theater is nothing more than an empty building.

response.speaker: Sharif
response.text: And without its performances, the theater has nothing else of value.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: What you said isn't true at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, keep it cool, Nilou!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: (Right, I need to keep calm, but he...)

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: (Just a little more. Zubayr Theater isn't just a performance venue to us...)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Zubayr Theater isn't simply a performance venue to us — it means more than that. It's been our home for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ms. Rekhar can't go on adventures anymore, but she has found a stable career and a new life at the theater.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Her son, Sohrin, has already passed his theater exam, and he'll soon be our newest member.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Khasani found a new way to look at art. He decided to stay at the theater to watch us grow.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Mr. Farhad and Mr. Hushang visit even when there isn't a show going on, and they always tell us lots of entertaining stories.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Even Inayah wants to stay with us, and she's starting to look forward to a new future.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Zubayr Theater exists for them... for every single one of us!

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Perhaps Zubayr Theater has provided you with a multitude of positive emotions and experiences. However, you have misconstrued something, young miss.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: The interpersonal relationships you speak of were established upon normal theater operations.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Sheikh Zubayr operates the theater for his livelihood, his employees work for their wages, and the audience comes to enjoy performances.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: Relationships are merely a byproduct in this exchange of interests. They may be pleasant and captivating, but they can only ever be secondary.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: When scholars collaborate to solve difficult problems, we freely share our knowledge and resources with one another, as if we were all kin.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: However, this collaboration ends after the results of our work are published.

dialogues.speaker: Sharif
dialogues.text: The reason is simple: We are scholars, and there are new projects that await our attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He really doesn't think much of relationships. Paimon also thinks he did a lot of prep — he's been solid as a rock.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: Sharif's argument is currently the more persuasive of the two for this point of contention.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: The continuance of the interpersonal relationships Nilou spoke of remains hypothetical before the theater's demolition, whereas the situation that Sharif described has been well documented at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Safwan
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has made significant academic contributions in no small part due to its researchers' efficiency and ability to compartmentalize.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, what should we do? Things are going in the opposite direction...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A set-up? So Nilou's got him?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: (Good, he's said what he said. The next argument could decide this debate.)

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: (But... is this really the best thing to do? It might be too cruel to Inayah...)

choices.text: Nilou might be setting him up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In the blink of an eye, it's already debate time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did a lot of preparations with Nilou! Hopefully they were helpful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you still worried about Inayah?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's be sure to come back often. Who knows, maybe things will have worked out for her!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Don't think that would make for a good rebuttal.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Nonono, can't do that.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (I need to rethink things. This is a crucial moment, so I can't mess up.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (No, Zubayr Theater should be...)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (I can't seem to make a connection here.)

dialogues.speaker: Rekhar
dialogues.text: The most important thing about an experience is how you choose to interpret it.

dialogues.speaker: Khasani
dialogues.text: Art must first be appreciated by others to confer value.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Mr. Zubayr has been meticulously managing the theater. Everything checks out.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Everyone is free to appreciate art — no form of art is inherently superior.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (Inayah really wants to win. She doesn't wanna lose anything else because of her painful past.)

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: (The theater carries everyone's feelings, and serves as the bond that connects us all.)
